report.summary: Chunk 2 of graph_delta.py: implements structure/type/ref extraction, measure(), run(), render(), main(), held_out().
risks: _structure_by_function | medium | The docstring claims the three signals are independent but the code only records node class names with depth; independence is not proven by this code alone. | Check if Name/Constant/Load/Store/Del are truly excluded from all three signals and if the depth-limited walk could miss structural differences.

_structure_keys | low | The function adds keys for each count n, but if counter is empty, the loop does nothing and returns empty set; this is fine but could be misinterpreted as 'no structure' vs 'no functions'. | Verify that empty counter is handled correctly by callers.

_type_edge_keys | medium | The function calls parse_mod.python_type_facts which is not defined in this chunk; if it raises AttributeError or SyntaxError, returns empty set. This is documented but the fallback could mask errors. | Ensure that the except clauses are not too broad and that callers handle empty set correctly.

measure | high | The function reads the target file, applies mutation in memory, and computes deltas for multiple layers. If the 'find' anchor is not present, it skips the mutation. This is correct but assumes the corpus is pinned to a revision; if the corpus drifts, mutations are silently skipped. | Confirm that the corpus revision is pinned and that skipped mutations are logged.

run | medium | The function aggregates results per defect class, but skipped mutants are not counted in total/detected/missed. This is documented but could be surprising. | Verify that callers understand the counting semantics.

main | high | The function has a comment about specificity and commit_shas being defined below the __name__ block, leading to a runtime error if --specificity is used before those definitions are loaded. The code attempts to import graph_delta as _self to resolve late bindings, but this is fragile. | Ensure that the late-binding import works correctly or restructure the code to avoid forward references.

held_out | medium | The function is defined but its body is truncated; the docstring claims it uses generate() from .mutate, but that import is not shown. The function may be incomplete. | Review the full definition of held_out to ensure it is complete and correct.
todos: Verify that _structure_by_function correctly handles functions without docstrings.
Check that _type_edge_keys works for languages without type vocabulary.
Ensure that the 'find' anchor in mutations is always present in the corpus revision.
Test the late-binding import in main() for the --specificity flag.
Review the held_out function for completeness and correctness.
Add unit tests for all public functions.
Document the expected behavior when parse_mod.python_type_facts is missing.

handoff.purpose: Implements structure and type edge extraction, measure(), run(), render(), main(), and held_out() functions.

symbols.name: _structure_by_function
symbols.note: Parses text into AST, walks functions, records structural node types with depth, returns dict of Counter per function name.

symbols.name: _structure_keys
symbols.note: Converts structure counter into a set of keys like fn:shape#i for each occurrence.

symbols.name: _units_and_refs
symbols.note: Extracts units and identifier references from text using spec and graph modules.

symbols.name: _type_edge_keys
symbols.note: Extracts type-layer edges from text using parse_mod.python_type_facts, returns set of keys.

symbols.name: measure
symbols.note: Applies one mutation in memory, computes deltas for leaky refs, AST refs, literals, structure, types, and data.literals layers.

symbols.name: run
symbols.note: Loads mutations, measures each, aggregates results per defect class, returns dict with version, counts, skipped, detected, missed, by_defect_class, results.

symbols.name: render
symbols.note: Formats the run result dict into a human-readable string.

symbols.name: main
symbols.note: CLI entry point: handles --held-out, --specificity, --json flags, writes results to runs/eval/graph_delta*.json.

symbols.name: held_out
symbols.note: Intended to generate a mechanically generated corpus and compute detection rate per operator; function body truncated in this chunk.

claims.text: Names and constants are the OTHER layers' business. Recording only the node class is what keeps the three signals independent.
claims.why: The claim about independence of three signals is not verifiable from this code alone; it references other layers not shown.
The code explicitly checks depth > 24 and returns early, acting as a guard against deeply nested nodes.

claims.text: Recording only the node class is what keeps the three signals independent.
claims.why: Cannot verify independence from this chunk alone; requires knowledge of other layers.

claims.text: Degrades to an empty set for a language with no type vocabulary — which is reported, never silently treated as 'nothing changed'.
claims.why: The function catches AttributeError and SyntaxError, returning an empty set. The docstring says this is reported, but the function itself just returns empty set; reporting is left to the caller.

claims.text: Apply one mutation IN MEMORY and report what moved. Nothing is written.
claims.why: The function reads the file, applies string replacement, computes deltas, and returns a DeltaResult without writing anything to disk.

claims.text: The corpus is pinned to a revision; a drifted anchor is a real finding about the corpus, not a licence to fuzzy-match into place.
claims.why: The code checks if mutation.find is in before text; if not, it sets skipped_reason and returns early, refusing to apply fuzzy matching.

claims.text: LEAKY arm: raw-source identifiers, comments included. Kept on purpose -- the gap between the two arms IS the measured size of the marker artefact.
claims.why: The leaky arm uses _units_and_refs which operates on raw text (comments included) and adds a LayerDelta for code.refs.leaky.

claims.text: CLEAN arm: AST identifiers. Comments are not tokens here.
claims.why: The clean arm uses _ast_refs which presumably parses AST and extracts identifiers; comments are excluded.

claims.text: Skipped mutants are NOT counted as misses and NOT counted as passes. An anchor that no longer matches means the corpus drifted; folding that into either column would turn a bookkeeping problem into a result.
claims.why: In run(), the skipped list is built separately from applied/detected/missed; applied filters out skipped mutations, and detected/missed only consider applied ones.

claims.text: MEASURED 2026-07-30: `specificity`, `commit_shas` and `measure_commit` are defined BELOW the `if __name__` block and this function is defined above them, so no committed command could reach the specificity arm at all.
claims.why: The comment describes a design issue where functions are defined after the main block, making them unreachable from the CLI. The code attempts to work around this with a late import, but the comment accurately describes the problem.

claims.text: Held out in the meaningful sense: :mod:`daedalus.eval.mutate` builds the corpus from the tree by rule, with no knowledge of what the scoring layers look at, so nothing here was tuned against these specific mutants.
claims.why: Cannot verify that mutate module builds corpus without knowledge of scoring layers; the import is not shown in this chunk.

claims.text: Scored on the CLEAN arm only. The three layers are applied to a function's source before and after mutation, and a mutant counts as detected if any of them moves.
claims.why: The body of held_out is truncated; cannot verify scoring logic from this chunk.

observations.what: _structure_by_function uses a depth limit of 24 to guard against malicious input.
_type_edge_keys returns empty set on AttributeError or SyntaxError, which may silently mask errors.
measure() reads the target file and applies mutation in memory; no disk writes.
run() aggregates results per defect class, but skipped mutations are excluded from counts.
main() attempts to resolve late bindings via import for --specificity flag, which is fragile.
held_out function is truncated in this chunk; its docstring references generate() from .mutate but the import is not shown.
